problems.text: Decision 4 is still not done for a refused confirmation (item 5 of the first check). `failed_summary_detail(.., None)` is called only from its own test (policy.rs:1780). The function is private to policy.rs and its one real caller, `missing_evidence_detail`, returns nothing unless the code is `label-evidence-missing`. The refused branch of `confirm` in ops.rs is unchanged: it prints `<F> confirm refused (<code>)` and the refusal message, with no reasons, limitation lines or per-capture values of the failed summaries. The refix report's sentence that the helper is 'used by ... a refused confirmation (all failed summaries)' is false. The test `a_refused_confirmation_prints_every_failed_summary_up_to_a_cap` checks the helper's filter and cap only, so its name describes behaviour that does not exist. Fix: call the helper from the refused branch of `confirm` and assert on the steps of a refused confirmation.

The row says `dla-bench dynamic` prints the failed-summary detail 'for a label refused for missing evidence and for a refused confirmation'. The second half is false (see the item above), and the row lists `a_refused_confirmation_prints_every_failed_summary_up_to_a_cap` among the tests of the correction. The row also says the three shim-limitation tests of the harness run 'each failed' with the hunk reverted; the refix report names two of them (the note test and the capture test), not `the_shim_counts_as_preloaded_only_with_the_shim_library_in_the_preload_variable`.

An argv word is cut to its last 28 characters before the redactor sees it, so a `key=value` word whose value has 27 characters or more loses its `key=` and is written as it is. It reaches the limitation line (ledger, and the CI log through `gate_detail`) and `captures[].argv_tail` of the raw file. Seen with the new binary and no raw-values consent: `--password=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzA` gives `kept pid 10872 (java shop.Main ...=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzA)`, and `-Djavax.net.ssl.keyStorePassword=changeit-changeit-changeit-prod` gives `...ngeit-changeit-changeit-prod`. A 26-character value is shaped (`...d=<26:a+:...>`). The test uses a 14-character value, so it passes. A secret given as its own word (`--token CorrectHorseBatteryStaple`) is not shaped either; that is how `Redactor::name` treats any text. Fix: pass each word through the redactor first, then cut.

Test gap on the second item of the first check. The test calls `split_shim` only, so it covers the early return without `--capture` but not the two `if capturing` guards around the removal of the stale `shim-dump.jsonl` at the start of a point. With either guard removed every test still passes and a run without `--capture` deletes the files again. The behaviour itself is right in a real run (see confirmed).

Chance identity, unchanged since the first check. In a hand-given or older file with several processes, when a process that is not the measured one has the capture's number in its argv and the measured one does not, the reader now reads the smaller process and writes no limitation line; HEAD read the larger one. Seen in three crafted cases: a helper `ninja -j 2220` beside `./prog`; a driver beside a helper with `--port <x>`; `x` of 1, 2, 3 with another process holding that token. In driver mode `x` is the step times all rounds (run.rs:1016 and 1728) and the driver's argv never holds it, so any match there is chance. Files the new harness writes hold one record and are not affected. A limitation line when identity chose among several processes would at least show the choice.

Wording. Two doc comments still say the detail gives 'the process each capture was read from'; `gate_detail` names the first capture and at most three captures the holder is absent from. Only `gate_detail`'s own comment was corrected. The comment on `failed_summary_detail` describes its use by a refused confirmation, which has no caller.

Two more differences from HEAD in crafted files, both by design and neither realistic. Two records of one pid: the last is read, HEAD read the larger (the shim writes one exit record per process). A program whose first argv word is a listed tool name (`./make 2220`): it is dropped as a tool even though it carries the count, and the other process is read with no limitation; `select_measured` has the same rule.

The cap of 8 detail lines cuts from the end. A failed summary lists its limitation lines before its holder lines, so with two failed summaries of 5 lines each the second one loses its `holder ...` and `records read from` lines and keeps its limitation lines. Both shim summaries read the same files, so the first one's holder lines carry the information.

The three other fixtures the brief named (native-vendor-codec, rust-private-registry, node-native-addon) are `impossible` fixtures that run no harness (`ran no`, 0 series), so their pass says nothing about this change. Of the 60 fixtures in the baseline only jni-order-codec uses the shim readers.

Two counts are swapped: `cargo test -p dla-workload --lib harness::` gives 146 passed (the report says 147) and the dla-bench lib tests 147 (the report says 146). The brief's `--lib` form for dla-cli fails with `no library targets found in package dla-cli`; `--bin dla` is the form that runs.
These two work directories (4 MB and 144 MB) are from my second bench runs with `--keep-work`. I left them because I may delete only under my scratch dir; they can be removed.

confirmed:
Four of the five problems of the first check are fixed and hold in real runs. The fifth (a refused confirmation) is not fixed although the refix report says it is, and one new problem turned up in the redaction. I edited no repository file.

ITEMS OF THE FIRST CHECK
1. False limitation on a harness without a shim: fixed. `shim_missing_note` returns nothing unless the manifest preloads libdlashim. In a kept run of python-report-memo-bounded the capturing run has 5 limitation lines, none about a shim record, and no point has a shim file. By reading, the note test and the capture test fail without the `preloaded` check.
2. A run without --capture deleting shim files: fixed. I took a snapshot of jni-order-codec right after its capture run, then ran `dla alloc-test H1 --finding jvm/F19` and `dla harness run H1 --iterations 1` in it. p1 and p2 got a new dump.jsonl (new pids); shim-dump.jsonl of p1 to p9 kept the capture run's records. The type-histogram-diff command of captures.json passed its gate before, between and after.
3. Unredacted argv in the limitation line: fixed for values up to 26 characters; longer ones still come through (third problem).
4. docs/VERIFY.md row: now the last row of the `## M7` table (line 522, the next heading is at 524), 4 cells, balanced backticks, no pipe in a code span, no plan names or line numbers. Its content has a false sentence (second problem).
5. Refused confirmation: not fixed (first problem).
Minor items: the cap and exact match in `gate_detail`, the raw-file fields asserted in the reader test, and the empty brackets are fixed (read; the brackets also seen in live output).

SELECTION RULE, 29 CRAFTED CASES
Built from the real records of p1 to p3 and run with both binaries. The older binary read by HEAD's rule (largest total, the later on a tie) in all 29.
- One process only (the program, the test JVM alone, a driver): same record as HEAD, no limitation.
- Two processes, neither argv has the count: same record as HEAD, plus a limitation line with the count, pid, argv words and both sizes.
- Measured process without a shim record: a lone other process is read silently, as at HEAD; with two others size decides and the limitation says so. The harness writes no file for such a point.
- Native dump with a build tool and the program: the tool is dropped by its first argv word or its exe, and the program is read even when the tool is four times larger or carries the count; HEAD read the tool. An unlisted tool (cmake) without the count: size and a limitation, same record as HEAD.
- Driver file: one process is read; with two, size and a limitation, same record as HEAD.
- No pid: identity still works. No argv: size and a limitation with no brackets, `pid ?` when the pid is missing too.
- Size deciding at each of 17 captures: 17 limitation lines per evidence record, exit 0.
Worse than HEAD only in the chance cases (minor) and the two by-design cases (note).

REPLAY OF THE REAL CASE
Cause figures are as reported: 41858379 and 47769802 at p1, 18908890 and 48416586 at p2, 19407935 and 144893809 at p17. I copied the 17 shim-dump.jsonl files into two fresh runs and doubled the test JVM's figures in p1 to 83716758.
- target/release/dla (2026-11-12): type-histogram-diff and alloc-stack-diff both fail with `nothing grows strictly across all 17 captures` and `stack:Java_shop_codec_Native_open: holder absent from dump 1`.
- target/debug/dla: both pass with `stack:Java_shop_codec_Native_open`; capture 1 is read from pid 10872 (`shop.codec.MainKt 2220`).

RUNS, ALL PASSING
- summarize_native 27, summarize_robust 6
- shim_groups unit tests 6 (with `--bin dla`)
- dla-workload `--lib harness::` 146
- dla-bench: 147 lib tests and every integration binary
- `dla schema --check`: ok, 20 checked
- clippy `-D warnings`, all targets, on dla-cli, dla-workload and dla-bench: clean
- rustfmt --check on the 8 Rust files of this pass: clean
- test_grade.py: 190 OK
- `cargo build -p dla-cli -p dla-bench`: up to date
- jni-order-codec, twice: pass, 1 confirmed, 5 refuted, leaks 2/2, same operations and summarize evidence as u8acc, both shim summaries `gate pass, tied jvm/F19`. Passed columns 16 and 14 against 14.
- python-report-memo-bounded, twice: pass. Refuted is 4 against 1 in u8acc because the unbound alloc-test now favors non-leak; that verdict comes from the other pass's files and is not worse for a control fixture.
- Kept jni directory: the capturing run has 19 limitation lines, none about a shim record; p1 to p9 hold one record each, the program's; p10 to p17 hold none; every command of captures.json finds its files.

CLAIMS OF THE REFIX REPORT
- Confirmed: items 1, 2 and 4; item 3 within the limit above; the `gate_detail` changes and its extended test; the raw-file assertion; the three run.rs tests; the replay with the older binary; the audit of other readers (my search found no other largest-among-processes choice, and no doc states the old rule); the checks listed above.
- False: that a refused confirmation prints the detail; decision 4 'done ... also for a refused confirmation'; the two swapped test counts.
- Unverified: see the next field.
